name: Movement Media and Insurgents
overview: The Movement Media and Insurgents bloc is defined by what its members own, not what they say: audiences outside the government. Carlson owns his network outright after buying out 1789 Capital and the other investors (Axios, Jun 2025). Bannon's War Room airs on Robert Sigg's Real America's Voice; the Mercers cut him off in 2018. Greene and Kent left office and are building a new-party lane with Carlson and Massie (Aug 2026).

Their slogans split by audience. On Iran, Kent resigned citing the war (Mar 17) and Carlson sells restraint, but Bannon told CPAC to "have his back" (Mar 27) and Loomer called war critics a "foreign influence operation" (Mar 3). Loomer, funded by Robert Shillman, depends on access to Trump, so she is re-homed with the Maximalists. Enforcement veterans (Bovino, Morgan, Howell) and the contractor Prince want posts and budget in the deportation machine, which is the Maximalists' interest, so they move there with a secondary row here. Hawley voted against the Iran war powers resolution and flips when the White House presses; he moves to the Party Machine.

Precedent (my reading): Pat Buchanan, a television commentator, ran an "America First" insurgency against a sitting Republican president in 1992, again in 1996, then took the Reform Party line in 2000 and won under one percent. The commentator-to-insurgent-to-third-party path maps onto Carlson, Greene, Kent and Massie: the anti-war line is the product and the leverage, and the exit threat pays only if the party buys it off before it is used.

IMM.title: Immigration

paras: Position.

Split by audience. Mar 17: Kent resigned, saying Iran posed no imminent threat. Carlson and Greene attack the war. Mar 3: Loomer called war critics a “foreign influence operation.” Mar 27: Bannon told CPAC “people got to have his back.” Hawley voted against the war powers resolution.
Why the faction does it. Each member sells the line its own audience buys. There is no shared stake in the outcome, only in staying the base’s voice (my reading).
Who and why.

Kent Posture: no new wars, blaming Israel’s lobby. Interest: the resignation cost him his job, the best costly evidence in the bloc, and bought him a place in Carlson’s new lane (he urged Carlson to run, Aug).
Carlson Posture: restraint. Interest: he owns his network, which cited “historic growth” from Iran coverage; restraint is his product and his 2028 leverage.

Bannon Posture: warns the war could break MAGA, yet backs Trump and wants Israel and Arab states to supply ground troops (Mar 30). Interest: a broker who never breaks with Trump keeps his access and his audience (my reading).
Loomer (home Maximalists) Posture: pro-war, pro-Israel. Interest: access to Trump is her asset, so she backs what Trump does.
Gabbard left May 22 citing her husband’s cancer, after defending the launch in office; she is no longer counted here.
Say versus do. Kent acted; the others spoke.

Stance audit. Kent resigned over the war, Carlson criticized it, and Loomer and Bannon backed Trump in different ways. Kent’s March 17 resignation supplies evidence of a costly commitment. Compare dated statements by individual. Audience, access, and succession influence can reward different positions. Shillman backs Loomer and Real America’s Voice distributes Bannon’s show. Score the split by actor. A shared audience market gives weak evidence of any individual’s motive.

paras: Position.
Demanded a forensic audit of MAGA Inc.; called Blair and LaCivita “grifters” (Oct 7).
Why the faction does it. Pressure on the Operation, which Bannon opposes and gains from weakening.
Who and why.

Bannon Motives: (1) Rivalry: the Operation sells proximity to Trump (see The Operation), and his own camp loses if that is the only route. (2) Timing: the demand came the day Trump said he would “terminate” conflicted consultants. Bannon wanted a review. (3) Ambition: he loses ground if Vance wins and gains if the Operation weakens (my reading).
Say versus do. The demand is a demand; no audit has been reported.
MID.title: Midterms

paras: Position.
June: Carlson will not back the GOP.
Bannon is “working on” a third term and calls Vance “not tough enough.”
Why the faction does it. A third term or a tougher heir keeps this faction’s leverage; a Vance win shrinks it.
Who and why.

Bannon Motives: (1) Ambition: allies say he pushes the third term because he wants to run himself (Axios), and he has a PAC and a “WarRoom: Texas” operation. He denies a run. (2) Product: he is helping Dershowitz with a third-term book, and the talk feeds his show. (3) Pressure: he presses Vance, Rubio (too close to Israel) and Cruz (Israel, AI bill) so that none becomes the heir without him (my reading).
Carlson Motives: Audience: his network cited “historic growth” from Iran war coverage (press release, Apr 30, 2026). Refusing to back the GOP fits an audience that distrusts the party.
Greene resigned from the House (reported). Motives: Circumstance: no stated plan; outside the party she has no constraints. No stake found.
Say versus do. “Working on” a third term is a statement.

why: Audience revenue, status, ideological influence, and the ability to mobilize voters are separate rewards. Shillman's backing of Loomer and Real America's Voice's distribution of Bannon's show enable different actors. Attribute funding, distribution, and policy pressure to the people involved.
